# 2 Kings Chapter 8 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 228v–229v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2KI_008_page_001.jpg, 2KI_008_page_002.jpg, 2KI_008_page_003.jpg

---

**8:1** And-Elisha spoke to the-woman whose-son he-had-restored-to-life [hecheyah], saying: Rise and-go [qumi ulekhi], you and-your-household, and-sojourn [veguri] wherever you-can-sojourn, for YHWH has-called for-a-famine [ra'av], and-it-shall-also come to the-land [for] seven years.

**8:2** And-rose the-woman and-did according-to-the-word of-the-man of-God, and-she-went, she and-her-household, and-sojourned in-the-land of-the-Pelishtim seven years.

**8:3** And-it-was at-the-end of-seven years, and-returned the-woman from-the-land of-the-Pelishtim, and-she-went-out to-cry-out [litso'q] to the-king for her-house and-for-her-field [sadah].

**8:4** And-the-king was-speaking to Gechazi, servant of-the-man of-God, saying: Tell [sapperah] me, please, all the-great-things [ha-gedolot] which Elisha has-done.

**8:5** And-it-was [as] he-was-telling the-king how he-had-restored-to-life the-dead [ha-met], and-behold, the-woman whose-son he-had-restored-to-life was-crying-out to the-king for her-house and-for-her-field. And-said Gechazi: My-lord the-king, this [is] the-woman and-this [is] her-son whom Elisha restored-to-life.

**8:6** And-asked the-king the-woman, and-she-told-him. And-appointed [vayitten] the-king for-her a-certain eunuch [saris], saying: Restore [hashev] all that [was] hers and-all the-yield [tevuot] of-the-field from-the-day she-left the-land until now.

**8:7** And-came Elisha to Dammeseq, and-Ben-Hadad king of-Aram was-sick [choleh]. And-it-was-told to-him, saying: The-man of-God has-come here [halom].

**8:8** And-said the-king to Chaza'el: Take in-your-hand a-gift [minchah] and-go to-meet the-man of-God, and-inquire [darashta] of-YHWH through-him, saying: Will-I-recover [ha-echyeh] from-this sickness [choli]?

**8:9** And-went Chaza'el to-meet-him, and-took a-gift in-his-hand, and-every-good-thing of-Dammeseq, a-load of-forty camels. And-he-came and-stood before-him and-said: Your-son Ben-Hadad, king of-Aram, has-sent-me to-you, saying: Will-I-recover from-this sickness?

**8:10** And-said Elisha to-him: Go, say [lekh emor]: You-shall-surely-recover [chayoh tichyeh]. But YHWH has-shown-me [hir'ani] that he-shall-surely-die [mot yamut].

**8:11** And-he-set [vaya'amed] his-face and-fixed-it [vayasem] until shame [bosh], and-wept the-man of-God.

**8:12** And-said Chaza'el: Why does-my-lord weep? And-he-said: Because I-know the-evil [ha-ra'ah] which you-shall-do to the-sons of-Yisra'el: their-fortresses [mibtsereyhem] you-shall-set on-fire [teshalleach ba-esh], and-their-young-men [bachureyhem] you-shall-kill with-the-sword, and-their-children [olleyhem] you-shall-dash-in-pieces [teratesh], and-their-pregnant-women [haroteyhem] you-shall-rip-open [tevaqqa'].

**8:13** And-said Chaza'el: But what [is] your-servant — the-dog [ha-kelev] — that he-should-do this great thing [ha-davar ha-gadol ha-zeh]? And-said Elisha: YHWH has-shown-me [hir'ani] you [as] king over Aram.

**8:14** And-he-went from Elisha and-came to his-master, and-he-said to-him: What did-Elisha say to-you? And-he-said: He-said to-me: You-shall-surely-recover [chayoh tichyeh].

**8:15** And-it-was on-the-next-day [mi-macharot], and-he-took the-coverlet [ha-makhber] and-dipped [vayitbol] [it] in-the-water and-spread [vayifros] [it] over his-face [al panav], and-he-died. And-reigned Chaza'el in-his-place [tachtav].

**8:16** And-in-the-fifth year of-Yoram son of-Ach'av, king of-Yisra'el — and-Yehoshafat [was] king of-Yehudah — began-to-reign [malakh] Yehoram son of-Yehoshafat, king of-Yehudah.

**8:17** A-son of-thirty-two years [was he] when-he-began-to-reign, and-eight years he-reigned in-Yerushalayim.

**8:18** And-he-walked in-the-way [be-derekh] of-the-kings of-Yisra'el, as the-house of-Ach'av had-done, for the-daughter of-Ach'av was his-wife [ishto]. And-he-did the-evil [ha-ra'] in-the-eyes of-YHWH.

**8:19** But YHWH was-not-willing [lo avah] to-destroy [lehashchit] Yehudah, for-the-sake of-David his-servant, as he-had-said [ki amar] to-give to-him a-lamp [nir] for-his-sons all the-days.

**8:20** In-his-days Edom revolted [pasha'] from-under the-hand of-Yehudah and-made-a-king [vayamliku] over-themselves a-king.

**8:21** And-crossed-over Yoram to-Tsa'ir, and-all the-chariots with-him. And-he-rose by-night and-struck Edom who-surrounded [ha-saviv] him, and-the-commanders of-the-chariots [sarey ha-rekhev], and-the-people fled to-their-tents.

**8:22** And-revolted Edom from-under the-hand of-Yehudah until this day. Then revolted Livnah at-that time.

**8:23** And-the-rest of-the-deeds [divrey] of-Yoram and-all that he-did, are-they-not written in-the-book of-the-chronicles of-the-kings of-Yehudah?

**8:24** And-lay-down [vayishkav] Yoram with-his-fathers and-was-buried with-his-fathers in-the-city of-David, and-reigned Achazyahu his-son in-his-place.

**8:25** In-the-twelfth year of-Yoram son of-Ach'av, king of-Yisra'el, began-to-reign Achazyahu son of-Yehoram, king of-Yehudah.

**8:26** A-son of-twenty-two years [was] Achazyahu when-he-began-to-reign, and-one year he-reigned in-Yerushalayim. And-the-name of-his-mother [was] Atalyahu, daughter [bat] of-Omri, king of-Yisra'el.

**8:27** And-he-walked in-the-way of-the-house of-Ach'av and-did the-evil in-the-eyes of-YHWH, like-the-house of-Ach'av, for he-was a-son-in-law [chatan] of-the-house of-Ach'av.

**8:28** And-he-went with-Yoram son of-Ach'av to-war against Chaza'el king of-Aram at-Ramot Gilead, and-the-Arameans struck [vayakku] Yoram.

**8:29** And-returned Yoram the-king to-heal [lehitrape'] in-Yizre'el from the-wounds [ha-makkot] which the-Arameans struck-him in-Ramah, when-he-fought against Chaza'el king of-Aram. And-Achazyahu son of-Yehoram, king of-Yehudah, went-down to-see Yoram son of-Ach'av in-Yizre'el, for he [was] sick [choleh].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 — "YHWH has called for a famine":** The Hebrew uses *qara'* (to call) — YHWH "summons" the famine as one summons a servant. The language personifies famine as an instrument of divine will. The Shunammite woman from chapters 4-5 reappears, her story framing Elisha's wider ministry.

**v.10 — The double oracle:** Elisha's response is deliberately ambiguous: "You shall surely recover" (*chayoh tichyeh*) — the illness is not fatal. "But YHWH has shown me that he shall surely die" (*mot yamut*) — he will die by another cause. The grammar separates the prognosis from the prophecy.

**v.11 — "until shame":** The Hebrew *ad bosh* means Elisha held his gaze until it became unbearable, shameful. Some read *ad bosh* as "beyond measure." The weeping follows — Elisha sees into Hazael's future and grieves for what Israel will suffer.

**v.15 — the coverlet:** The *makhber* (thick cloth/coverlet) soaked in water and placed over Ben-hadad's face is an act of suffocation. Hazael murders his master while telling him the prophet said he would recover. The irony is lethal: the true oracle was "he shall surely die."

**v.26 — "daughter of Omri":** Athaliah is called "daughter of Omri" though she was likely Ahab's daughter (Omri's granddaughter). Hebrew *bat* can mean "descendant." The point is dynastic: Omri's house infects Judah through marriage.

*— EMET*
